Theme

Latin word

ultrā

ultrā (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative; also an adverb · Wiktionary

beyond, further than; further, beyond; any further

In this lexicon

  • beyond

    the recommended word · classical · Quint. 11.2.13: vix eō ultrā līmen ēgressō; Tac. Agr. 30.5: nūlla jam ultrā gēns; Traupman 202; Traupman 206; Traupman 279

  • further

    also used · classical · Quint. 2.3.7: nec prōcēdat ultrā quam comes possit; Tac. Agr. 30.5: nūlla jam ultrā gēns

Examples

  • nam vix eō ultrā līmen ēgressō, trīclīnium illud suprā convīvās corruit

    for he had hardly stepped beyond the threshold when that dining room fell in on the guestsQuint. 11.2.13

    In the entry for beyond

  • nūlla jam ultrā gēns, nihil nisi flūctūs et saxa

    there is no people beyond us now, nothing but waves and rocksTac. Agr. 30.5

    In the entry for beyond

  • pergeret porrō īre nec ultrā inquīreret

    he should go on further and ask no moreLiv. 21.22.9

    In the entry for beyond

  • illīs īra modum suprā est

    their anger is beyond measureVerg. G. 4.236

    In the entry for beyond

  • ut vēlōcissimus quoque, sī forte iter cum parvulō faciat, det manum et gradum suum minuat nec prōcēdat ultrā quam comes possit

    as even the fastest walker, if he happens to be travelling with a little child, gives him his hand, shortens his stride and goes no further than his companion canQuint. 2.3.7
